    #16197. Trust Is The Fresh Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (916 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Trust Is The Fresh Battleground For Customer Engagement

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.
    • ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult.
    • Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Garvert is the EVP of Fraud & Communications Solutions for TransUnion.

    ​Engaging with consumers has never been more essential, or more difficult. Amid the meteoric rise of AI-enabled scams, call spoofing and social engineering attacks, the challenges organizations face when trying to reach consumers seem insurmountable.

    Every interaction depends on trust, yet consumers are more hesitant than ever to engage. Many of the traditional warning signs consumers were trained to recognize have disappeared—consumers are on edge.

    And with good reason: It’s a jungle out there.

    In our recent global study, “61% of business leaders ranked fraud among the risks with the greatest potential business impact, ahead of cybersecurity breaches, compliance, customer churn, operational cost and reputational risk. More concerning, 58% stated they’re very or extremely concerned fraud is evolving faster than their organizations’ abilities to detect and prevent it.”.

    Sources indicate that historically, organizations have viewed fraud and engaging with customers as separate disciplines. But today’s threat environment makes it clear they’re deeply interconnected. In many cases, the communication channel itself—whether a phone call, text message, email or mobile app interaction—provides the first indication that fraud may be occurring.

    Consumers don’t experience fraud, identity and communication challenges as separate issues. To them, it’s one experience, one problem. It’s a trust problem that’s reshaping the customer journey. In fact, 69% of consumers say they would switch vendors for stronger security.

    Trust has become the foundation for both customer engagement and fraud prevention.

    At our recent Fraud & Communications Summit in Chicago, keynote speaker Matt O’Neill, a former U.S. Secret Service Special Agent and recipient of Gold and Silver Awards for distinguished service, shared insights from years spent working undercover as a banker, broker, money launderer and other personas. In these roles, he led multinational investigations into crypto-laundering networks and dark web marketplaces.

    According to O’Neill, fraudsters are winning because fraud has evolved into a highly organized industry. He explained that scam operations now function much like large multinational corporations. Scam compounds are similar to call centers, complete with organizational structures, performance quotas, shift schedules and human resources departments. Unfortunately, many of these compounds operate under sophisticated criminal networks and employ workers who have been trafficked.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, the barrier to entry into the fraud world has never been lower. AI enables fraudsters to create convincing scams at scale in virtually any language, including cloned voices, deepfake videos and personalized social engineering campaigns. And it’s cheap.​.

    Industry observers note that the consequences of eroding trust extend well beyond fraud losses. Organizations often experience:.

    • Reduced marketing effectiveness.

    Ironically, the industries and brands most trusted by consumers are frequently among the most targeted by fraudsters, with the highest fraud instances related to auto lending, bank-issued and retail credit cards and unsecured personal lending.

    According to Edelman, trust now rivals price and quality as a primary factor influencing consumer decision-making. Research demonstrates that “77% of consumers cited confidence their personal data is secure as the most important feature when choosing whom to transact with online.”.

    Organizations can strengthen trust by approaching fraud prevention and customer communications as a unified strategy.

    According to recent reports, traditional fraud controls were designed for predictable attacks. Today’s fraudsters adapt quickly, vary their tactics and coordinate attacks across multiple channels and sessions. Identity verification remains important, but it only confirms who someone claims to be. It doesn’t determine whether the current interaction should be trusted.

    Here’s where identity verification falls short:.

    • KYC (Know Your Customer) controls are often strongest at onboarding, not throughout the customer lifecycle.

    • Devices, behaviors and risk profiles change over time.

    • Credentials can be compromised after verification.

    • Synthetic identities can appear legitimate on paper.

    The most vital fraud signal is often not a single event. Any single signal can be manipulated or generate false positives. It’s the story that unfolds throughout an interaction. It emerges through relationships among users, devices, accounts, entities and sessions.

    As if it wasn’t hard enough, AI has turbocharged fraud. In addition, labeling identified threats as AI-driven remains a challenge. That’s because it’s difficult to build comprehensive strategies with new AI fraud models evolving so rapidly.

    Industry observers note that while fraud practitioners know when an account was taken over, there’s currently no label for how it was taken over and whether AI drove the attack. As a result, the AI-attributed training set doesn’t exist yet for tracking that fraud, and detection stays anchored to heuristics and analyst judgment.

    To be able to engage effectively with consumers and prevent fraud, organizations must adopt continuous authentication and layered risk strategies.

    • Develop a comprehensive strategy—don’t address fraud in silos across your organization.

    • Form strategic partnerships with your cyber teams.

    • Correlate identity, device, behavioral and contextual signals in real time.

    The process is straightforward: Collect. Correlate. Score. Decide.

    It has been revealed that every phone call, text message, email and digital transaction represents a trust moment. Customers want confidence the organization contacting them is legitimate and their information and transactions are protected. Simply asking consumers to “trust us” is no longer enough.

    Verified identity, authenticated communications and real-time risk intelligence are becoming the foundation of trust in a digital-first world.

    The future isn’t reactive fraud mitigation. It’s proactive trust at the point of interaction, by orchestrating identity, risk and communications intelligence across every customer interaction.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 20, 2026 at 1:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bloom Energy ›.

    Recent findings suggest that bloom Energy (BE -13.97%), a developer of solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), was once considered a niche green energy stock. But over the past two years, its stock has rallied more than 530% as the data center market's rapid expansion generated strong tailwinds for its business. Bloom was also added to the S&P 500 (^GSPC -2.43%) this September.

    Bloom's SOFCs can convert natural gas, biogas, propane, and hydrogen into electricity without any combustion. Its systems can often be deployed in less than two months and bypass traditional utilities that often require years to set up new connections. Its new Power Connect System could further reduce its on-site installation time by over 40%.

    Sources indicate that A growing number of data center operators -- including Oracle (NASDAQ:ORCL), CoreWeave (CRWV -11.27%), Nebius (NBIS -13.77%), and Equinix (EQIX -3.25%) -- are using Bloom's SOFC systems to expand their AI infrastructure. That's why its backlog hit $20 billion at the end of 2025, and why it expects its revenue to more than double from $2.0 billion in 2025 to at least $4.4 billion in 2026. But will its stock head even higher over the next five years?

    From 2020 to 2025, Bloom's revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) increased at CAGRs of 23% and 82%, respectively.

    NYSE · As of 2:15 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, but from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Bloom's revenue and adjusted EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 73% and 126%, respectively. With an enterprise value of $50 billion, it still looks like a bargain at 25 times next year's adjusted EBITDA.

    Recent findings suggest that however, that's mainly because Bloom's stock has pulled back more than 50% from its all-time high of $345.85 on June 22, 2026. That pullback can be attributed to the Fed's rate hike in September, which made it more expensive to fund newly introduced data center projects; a major delay at Oracle's Project Jupiter AI data center campus; and a short-seller's allegations that Bloom's supply chain was dependent on China. The Democratic sweep of the midterm elections could also throttle the construction of new data centers with tighter regulations.

    According to recent reports, those challenges compressed Bloom's valuations, but its longer-term catalysts remain intact. The data center market is still growing, and tighter environmental restrictions could actually boost its sales of SOFC systems. Oracle should get Project Jupiter back on track, Bloom has directly refuted the short-seller's claims, and it's gradually expanding into more non-AI markets. Bloom's free cash flow -- which turned negative in the third quarter of 2026 after four consecutive quarters in positive territory -- should improve as those tailwinds kick in.

    If Bloom matches analysts' estimates through 2028, grows its adjusted EBITDA at a 25% CAGR through 2031, and trades at a more generous 20 times its current-year adjusted EBITDA by the final year, its stock price could rise more than 145% over the next five years.

    By Rich Smith – Nov 20, 2026 at 1:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Firefly Aerospace ›.

    Firefly Aerospace (FLY -9.12%) stock tumbled 9.6% through 12:50 p.m. ET Friday after investment banker JPMorgan cut its price target on the space stock by 20% to $32 per share.

    That's the bad news. The good news is that there doesn't appear to be any specific catalyst behind JP's price target reduction. The write-up on StreetInsider.com contains no worrisome details that would support the idea that Firefly stock is worth 20% less today than it cost yesterday -- and JP still believes the stock should be "overweight" in investor portfolios.

    Of course, the other bad news is that, even without a full explanation from JPMorgan, investors may reasonably question whether Firefly is worth the $32 the analyst indicates it is -- or even the $18 per share Firefly stock costs today!

    Recent findings suggest that recall that part of the reason Firefly stock is so expensive right now is that two weeks ago, Firefly inked a deal to sell 36 rocket engines to AST SpaceMobile (ASTS -8.71%) and help AST learn how to build rocketships. In exchange, AST would pay Firefly $1.3 billion.

    As I've already pointed out, however, this deal isn't all it's cracked up to be.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:16 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For one thing, only the first $400 million of this $1.3 billion appears to be guaranteed to be paid in cash. At least $400 million more will be paid in AST stock -- stock that is already down 28% since this deal was unveiled.

    According to recent reports, the form of payment for an additional $500 million, due upon delivery of engines and provision of engineering services, is unclear. It's probably supposed to be paid in cash, but the companies didn't state this outright in their press release.

    If any more of this is payable in rapidly devaluing AST stock, this deal could be worth far less to Firefly than investors expect.

    Costco’s Upcoming $30 Special Dividend Is Twice the Size of Its Last Special Payout. Is This the Most Unstoppable Consumer Staples Stock to Buy Now?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that earlier this month, Costco Wholesale (COST +1.46%) declared a special dividend of $30 per share, payable on Dec.
    • But rather than being a reason to buy the stock on its own, these intermittent bonus distributions point to a broader case for holding Costco as a long-term investment.
    • The special dividend payout is a way to reward its shareholders.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Nov 20, 2026 at 1:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Costco Wholesale ›.

    Sources indicate that earlier this month, Costco Wholesale (COST +1.46%) declared a special dividend of $30 per share, payable on Dec. 4 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on Nov. 24. That payout will be double the $15 per share special dividend that shareholders received in 2024.

    But rather than being a reason to buy the stock on its own, these intermittent bonus distributions point to a broader case for holding Costco as a long-term investment.

    The special dividend payout is a way to reward its shareholders. But it's also an indication that Costco has more money than it can usefully deploy to grow the business at the moment, a situation many companies would like to be in.

    In a recent development, for Costco, that situation has resulted from an increase in its income from membership sales, strong renewal rates, expansion, and improved profitability, which are all solid reasons to consider owning the stock. In its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, which ended Aug. 30, Costco reported membership income growth of 7.3%. That’s the revenue stream that makes the entire business work. Its product sales have extremely thin margins; Costco makes the bulk of its money on the membership fees, so growth on that line indicates healthy demand from customers wanting to access Costco's warehouses.

    In North America, Costco has a 92.3% membership renewal rate, while global renewals overall are just under 90%. This gives it a predictable high-margin revenue stream, and it also means Costco doesn't have to constantly replace large numbers of members who cancel. It also demonstrates that, despite concerns about rising grocery and household costs, most members still see enough value in the warehouse giant to keep their memberships. And if the economy were to enter a downturn, Costco offers the kind of deals on bulk goods that people particularly desire when their budgets get tighter.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:13 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that costco can also generate more revenue and translate it into profitability by opening upcoming warehouse stores. It chooses its locations selectively, as evidenced by the fact that it only opened 25 new warehouses in fiscal 2026. That selectivity is a positive, as expansion continues to drive membership fee growth without tying up all the cash Costco generates, giving it greater financial flexibility.

    It has been revealed that finally, the company can pay out this latest special dividend because it's simply turning more of its sales into profits. For fiscal 2026, Costco reported $9.2 billion in net income, a nearly 14% increase from the prior year.

    Costco's strong business model is what is allowing it to pay out that $30 special dividend, and it is one of the best consumer staples stocks on the market. But the clear strength of that business model has led the market to price high expectations into its stock.

    Trading at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 48.6, there's little room for Costco to deliver any underwhelming or mediocre results in its earnings reports. I still like Costco as a long-term portfolio addition, but investors should buy in with the understanding that the company has high expectations to live up to.

    #16180. When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1313 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    When To End A Technology Pilot: 19 Warning Signs

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1313 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test upcoming solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout.
    • For tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question.
    • A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Technology pilots give organizations an opportunity to test upcoming solutions on a limited scale, evaluate their potential and identify challenges before committing to a broader rollout. But not every pilot warrants further investment, and knowing when to end one can be just as key as knowing when to expand it.

    For tech leaders, the challenge is distinguishing between setbacks that can be addressed by adjusting a pilot’s scope or timeline and more fundamental issues that call its viability into question. Below, members of Forbes Technology Council share warning signs that indicate it’s time to end a technology pilot rather than extend it, redesign it or move it into production.

    A pilot without success criteria is not a pilot. Defining boundaries and expectations, and, importantly, being transparent, are critical to a pilot’s success. Owners should also share any uncertainty during the pilot instead of waiting for it to pivot or improve. - Arunava Sen, Tata Communications America Inc.

    Recent findings suggest that A clear sign is when the pilot team cannot tell you what the technology accessed, what decisions it made, or what data it touched. If you cannot answer those questions in a controlled environment (test group), you will not answer them in production. - Michael Nicosia, Salt Security.

    Sources indicate that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    One sign a technology pilot shouldn’t progress doesn’t involve the latest tech itself but the tools teams already work with. If teams are working in siloed workflows with tools that don’t collaborate with one another, introducing new technology can drive up costs, increase complexity and hurt productivity. Connected tools and workflows are integral to the success of any new tech deployment. - Usman Shuja, Bluebeam.

    End a pilot when its success depends on hand-curated data that won’t exist in production. If someone cleaned the dataset, resolved definitions and fixed edge cases for the pilot, and no one owns doing that at scale in production, extending or redesigning the product in production won’t help. In many cases, technology isn’t the problem; the foundation is. Ask not whether the pilot worked, but what it worked on. - Prakash Reddy, Okta.

    If the pilot only works while its champion is in the room or while the vendor quietly does manual work behind the scenes, you’ve tested enthusiasm, not technology. Hand it to a team that didn’t build it for 30 days. If results collapse, you’d be pushing a dependency into production, not a tool. End it and keep the learnings. - Damian Wasserman, BEON.tech.

    In a recent development, when the team stops asking what we learned and starts asking when we get to stop, that’s the sign. A pilot without defined success criteria is avoidance. If you can’t name the specific business result it was supposed to prove or disprove, extending it won’t help. End it, define the outcome you actually need, and redesign around that from the start. - Ali Alkhafaji, APPLY.

    It has been revealed that organizations should end a technology pilot when they have full visibility of the tool’s usage and cost metrics but still cannot connect either to a meaningful business outcome. Adoption alone is not enough without a clear path to measurable value, and extending the pilot risks turning experimentation into ongoing spend without a business case. - Conal Gallagher, Flexera.

    It has been revealed that A clear sign is when the people who were supposed to benefit stop asking about it. Pilots drag on because the sponsors like the idea, not because customers need it. If the pilot group has quietly gone back to their old way of working and nobody complains when the tool goes down, there’s nothing to extend. Name the lesson, thank the team and end it. - Hastimal Jangid, Coozmoo Digital Solutions, Inc.

    A pilot should be reconsidered when it performs well in a demo but can’t prove that it solves a real business problem. AI makes it easy to add capabilities, but more features don’t always mean more value. Teams need clear measures of success and feedback loops to understand what’s working and what’s not before investing further. - Tony Grout, M-Files.

    A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when it repeatedly fails to demonstrate measurable business value despite validated assumptions and reasonable adjustments. If the solution cannot deliver meaningful ROI, operational efficiency or strategic impact, extending it only increases sunk costs. Strong leadership means knowing when to stop, not just when to scale. - Kameshwar Singh, Cohesity.

    In a recent development, end a pilot if no effort was spent defining the vision and how value will be realized at scale. That’s like building a bridge from both ends without deciding where it should meet. - Venky Ramesh, LatentView Analytics.

    In a recent development, A pilot should end when success depends on conditions that production will never have: handpicked data, expert users, manual fixes, privileged integrations or constant vendor support. If removing that scaffolding collapses the value case, extending the pilot only perfects the illusion. The real test is not, “Does it work?” but, “Does it still create measurable value when exposed to ordinary users, messy data, real constraints and an ordinary day?” - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    End a pilot when making the technology operable, reliable and governable outweighs its business value. If protecting sensitive data, maintaining an audit trail and providing human oversight would cost more than the expected benefit, extending that particular pilot needs a stronger business case than the time and money already invested. - Brian Stimpfl, S-Docs.

    End a pilot when the evidence invalidates its core business premise. If customers can complete the workflow but gain no meaningful time, cost or quality improvement over the current process, more engineering won’t create demand. Define that minimum benefit before launch, test it with real users, and stop when it remains out of reach. - Irina Shymko, Langate Software.

    End the pilot when the team cannot define a credible path from the experiment to a measurable business outcome. If success still depends on vague future improvements, heroic manual support or assumptions the pilot was supposed to validate, extending it usually just delays the decision. - Dhyey Mavani, Abridge.

    It has been revealed that A pilot should end when the team cannot explain what new evidence another extension will produce. Every extra week should answer a specific open question about value, risk, adoption, cost or scale. Once the remaining time is only keeping the pilot alive, the experiment has already delivered its answer. - Sibasis Padhi, Walmart Inc.

    Sources indicate that I would end a pilot when it successfully completes individual tasks but repeatedly fails to deliver the full business outcome. Often, the underlying problem is the absence of a clear decision model for handling exceptions, approvals or unresolved work across teams. If nobody can authorize what happens next, scaling the technology only scales the problem. - Vamshi Noothi, Cisco.

    Industry observers note that A pilot should be ended if nobody uses it unless someone reminds them. A pilot that only stays alive while its sponsor keeps pushing won’t survive production, and extending it just postpones that answer. Software nobody uses isn’t free; it still costs money to run, maintain and support. End it, write down what you learned about the problem, and put the team on something people actually want. - Jeremy Suriel, Kustomer.

    In a recent development, A clear sign to end a technology pilot is when no business owner is willing to take responsibility for implementation. Even if the technology performs well, success requires business ownership, accountability and commitment to change. Without a sponsor willing to champion the solution, allocate resources and own the outcomes, extending the pilot is unlikely to deliver value. Technology cannot create lasting benefits without clear business ownership. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

Nvidia (NVDA -8.84%) dropped 37%, Micron Technology (MU -12.23%) is off by 33%, and Alphabet (GOOG -0.70%) (GOOGL -0.47%) is down 20%.

    Sources indicate that it hasn't been pretty. But analyst Dan Ives, a partner at Yorkville Ives, isn't abandoning his bullish outlook. In a post on X on Friday, Ives identified seven factors contributing to "a perfect storm" that's driving the sell-off.

    And here's the most vital part of his message: "The $4 trillion AI build-out is still happening," he wrote, "and our tech thesis into 2027 remains.".

    According to recent reports, that's key -- particularly for investors who are nervous about their portfolios right now. And if Ives is right, this is also an opportunity to buy tech stocks at a discount.

    Sources indicate that dan Ives. Image source: Getty Images.

    In his social media post, Ives noted the Democrats' midterm election victory is creating uncertainty for AI stocks, as investors worry that Washington will impose tougher restrictions on AI development and data center construction.

    He also singled out the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang "in his black eye moment." Huang was forced out after the board began investigating his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence officials believe was spying for Beijing.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:16 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that meanwhile, regulatory concerns involving China, persistent inflation, and the prospect of additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases have weighed on technology stocks. Ives also pointed to forced selling and investment funds suffering losses that have reduced their ability to buy shares.

    Ives even singled out Anthropic's (ANT -10.53%) successful IPO on Nov. 19, speculating that investors shifted money out of tech stocks and into the newly public AI organization.

    Recent findings suggest that A perfect storm, indeed. But here's the thing -- none of those factors mean that customers are slowing their AI spending. And the demand for computing capacity remains sky-high.

    That's why analysts, including Ives, have projected that capital expenditures and AI spending will reach $4 trillion.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:14 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that nvidia reported $115.8 billion in revenue in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, up 103% from a year ago. And data center revenue was $107.6 billion, up 110%. But perhaps the most crucial thing is that Nvidia increased its forecast for fiscal 2028 revenue growth from 70% to 75%. And notably, that outlook came in the first earnings report since Huang's departure. Management expects demand to accelerate even faster.

    Alphabet is seeing similar strength in cloud computing. Google Cloud revenue in the third quarter was $30.7 billion, up 103% from a year ago. Operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, and its backlog reached $561 billion.

    Those figures suggest businesses are still signing contracts for computing infrastructure, even as investors question whether AI spending has gone too far.

    According to recent reports, and Anthropic's IPO prospectus offers another example. The Claude developer has committed to spending at least $110 billion with Amazon (AMZN -3.32%) and $121.3 billion with Google under long-term cloud computing arrangements.

    That's an enormous amount of planned infrastructure spending from just one AI company.

    Ives can't predict when the technology sell-off will end. But his central argument deserves attention: The market's enthusiasm for AI stocks has cooled considerably, while the companies supplying the infrastructure continue to report massive demand.

    Buckle (BKE +6.63%) reported third quarter net income of $48 million, maintaining profitability despite unseasonably warm weather that impacted early denim sales. Management reported a 2.6% increase in net sales, supported by significant growth in the women's and kids segments and a shift toward new fashion silhouettes. The company continued its strategic expansion into premium and outlet centers, completing 14 new store openings year to date while managing merchandise margins through reduced markdowns and private label growth. Operating margins were pressured by increased labor and marketing costs, but the company ended the quarter with $332.2 million in total cash and investments.

    Operator: Good morning. Thank you for standing by, and welcome to Buckle's Third Quarter Earnings Release Webcast. [Operator Instructions] Members of Buckle's management on the call today are Dennis Nelson, President and CEO; Tom Heacock, Senior Vice President of Finance, Treasurer and CFO; Adam Akerson, Vice President of Finance and Corporate Controller; and Brady Fritz, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. Before beginning, the tech giant would like to reiterate its policy of not providing future sales or earnings guidance. All forward-looking statements made on the call are pursuant to the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Any unauthorized reproductions or recordings of the calls should not be relied upon as the information may be inaccurate. As a reminder, today's webcast is being recorded. And I'd now like to turn the conference over to your host, Tom Heacock.

Our November 20, 2026 press release reported that net income for the 13-week third quarter, which ended October 31, 2026, was $48 million or $0.94 per share on a diluted basis compared to net income of $48.7 million or $0.96 per share on a diluted basis for the prior year 13-week third quarter which ended November 1, 2025. Year-to-date, net income for the 39-week period ended October 31, 2026, was $139.3 million or $2.73 per share on a diluted basis which compares to net income of $128.9 million or $2.55 per share on a diluted basis for the prior year 39-week period ended November 1, 2025.

    Net sales for the 13-week third quarter increased 2.6% to $329.2 million compared to net sales of $320.8 million for the prior year 13-week third quarter. Comparable store sales for the quarter increased 0.6% in comparison to the same 13-week period in the prior year, and our online sales decreased 1.4% to $52.2 million. Year-to-date net sales increased 4.3% to $937.8 million compared to net sales of $898.7 million for the prior year 39-week fiscal period. Comparable store sales for the year-to-date period increased 2.5% in comparison to the same 39-week period in the prior year, and our online sales increased 1.1% to $144.5 million.

    Recent findings suggest that for the quarter, UPTs decreased approximately 0.5%, the average unit retail increased approximately 3% and the average transaction value increased about 2.5%. Year-to-date, UPTs decreased approximately 0.5%, the average unit retail increased approximately 4% and the average transaction value increased approximately 3%. Gross margin for the quarter was 47.8%, down 20 basis points from 48% in the third quarter of 2025. The decline was driven by a 60 basis point increase in buying, distribution and occupancy costs, primarily related to continued growth in the number of both newly introduced and remodeled store locations, and this increase was partially offset by a 40 basis point improvement in merchandise margin.

    Sources indicate that year-to-date gross margin was 47.3%, down 10 basis points from 47.4% for the same period last year. And again, the year-to-date decline was the result of a 60 basis point increase in buying distribution and occupancy expenses, partially offset by a 50 basis point increase in merchandise margin. Selling, general and administrative expenses for the quarter were 29.8% of sales compared to 29% for the third quarter of 2025. And for the year-to-date period, SG&A was 28.7% of net sales compared to 29.5% for the same period in the prior year.

    The third quarter increase was due to a 40 basis point impact from compensation expense related to realized gains on our deferred compensation proposal investments which was equally offset by investment income recognized in other income and also to a 35 basis point increase related to continued marketing investments, a 25 basis point increase in store labor related expenses and a 10 basis point increase in certain other SG&A expenses. And these increases were partially offset by a 30 basis point reduction in incentive and equity compensation accruals. Our operating margin for the quarter was 18% compared to 19% for the third quarter of fiscal 2025.

    Recent findings suggest that and for the year-to-date period, our operating margin was 18.6% compared to 17.9% for the same period last year. Income tax expense as a percentage of pretax net income for each of the current and prior year quarter and year-to-date periods was 24.5%. Our press release also included a balance sheet as of October 31, 2026, which included the following: inventory of $180.5 million, which was up 8.9% from the same time a year ago, and $332.2 million of total cash and investments. We ended the quarter with $195 million in fixed assets, net of accumulated depreciation. Our capital expenditures for the quarter were $10.8 million, and depreciation expense was $7.2 million.

    Sources indicate that for the year-to-date period, capital expenditures were $55.3 million and depreciation expense was $20.6 million. Year-to-date capital spending is broken down as follows: $34.1 million for new store construction, store remodels and technology upgrades and $21.2 million for capital spending at the corporate headquarters and distribution center. During the quarter, we opened 4 new stores and completed 4 full store remodels, one of which was a relocation to a new shopping center. And following quarter end, we opened 2 additional new stores which brings our year-to-date counts through today to 14 new stores, 14 full remodels and 2 store closures.

    It has been revealed that for the remainder of the year, we now anticipate completing 2 additional full remodeling projects, both of which will be completed in January. Buckle ended the quarter with 450 retail stores in 42 states compared to 442 stores in 42 states at the end of the third quarter of 2025. And now I'll turn it over to Adam Akerson, Vice President of Finance.

The women's business represented 52% of total sales for the quarter up from 51% last year. The biggest win in denim was the continued shift into fresh silhouettes. Wide-leg is now our largest women's denim fit, while barrel and low-rise styles also grew rapidly. Total women's denim sales were down about 0.5% against a 17.5% increase last year, with average denim price points increasing from $86.95 to $92.15 during the quarter.

    That same shift in silhouettes also drove the fashion pants category, our fastest-growing segment of the women's business, which was up nearly 60% year-over-year. This expanding category gives us a second path to earn our guest business as she looks to fill in her wardrobe beyond traditional denim. Combined with denim, total full-length women's bottoms for the quarter were up 3.5%. Women's tops grew approximately 4.5%, led by fashions, prints and graphics, along with strong growth in bralettes and sleeveless styles. In tops, our private brands did much of the work, growing 16% and highlighted by performance in BKE, Buckle Black, Willow & Root, and Gilded Intent.

    Industry observers note that our men's business increased approximately 0.5% for the quarter, representing 48% of total organization sales compared to 49% last year. Men's denim sales declined approximately 5% year-over-year. We are pleased with the response to relaxed fits, which grew double digits as demand shifted away from slimmer fits. Average denim price points increased from $88.15 to $88.40 for the quarter. We also saw unseasonably strong performance in our shorts selection throughout the quarter. Men's tops continued its strong growth trend within the men's business, increasing approximately 6% year-over-year.

    Our expanded polo assortment, short-sleeve, button-fronts, quarter-zips, hoodies and fashion solids each showed strong growth for the quarter. Graphic tees, which is our largest men's tops category also continued to grow. On a combined basis, accessory sales for the quarter increased approximately 1% against the prior year, while footwear sales decreased about 3%. These 2 categories accounted for approximately 10% and 4%, respectively, of third quarter net sales. This compares to 10% and 4.5%, respectively, for the third quarter of fiscal 2025. For the quarter, average accessory price points were up approximately 4.5%, and average footwear price points were up 8.5%.

    Recent findings suggest that our kids business delivered another outstanding quarter, increasing 14% on top of a 22% increase a year ago as it remains one of our consistent growth engines. Growth was led by denim, casual and knit bottoms, tees and hoodies. The same silhouette and wash trends driving our adult business resonated with kids and parents alike. For the quarter, denim accounted for approximately 43.5% of sales, and tops accounted for approximately 30%, which compares to 46% and 29% for each in the third quarter of fiscal 2025. Our private label business for the quarter represented 48% of sales versus 47.5% in the third quarter of 2025. And with that, we welcome your questions.

On merchandise margins, I mean, it truly was growth in merchandise margins like we've seen in several of the last quarters.     But true merchandise margins were up 30 basis points for the quarter, and that was really -- private label grew a little bit, markdowns were down and then just better pricing on some of our products, so kind of a combination of factors that really help drive that and reach really strong margin levels like we have over the last several quarters.

    Sources indicate that mauricio Serna Vega: Got it. And then just a quick follow-up just on the weather. We've heard from other retailers that end of October and coming into November unseasonably warm weather has affected, I guess, at the beginning of what you would call like the holiday season. So just any thoughts on how weather is impacting your business, especially at the start of November, the first couple of weeks?

    Thomas Heacock: I think we don't like to talk about weather a whole lot, but it certainly had an impact in Q3. And so I think when you look at broad chunks of the country and especially, weather, it was unseasonably warm. So I think that impacted to some degree, our denim business as we move through the quarter and then at least here in the Midwest, and now it's more seasonably cool and so more appropriate for what it would be for this time of the year. So it hasn't had much of an impact lately, but certainly did impact denim sales earlier in the quarter.

    Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our next question comes from Jon with Kansas City Capital.

    Jon Braatz: Dennis, I have a question. You're opening, I think, what, 12, 14 stores this year. What are your thoughts on next year? And it looks like the latest stores this year, a little bit of a drag on earnings. Would you anticipate that to reverse a little bit in year 2?

    Dennis Nelson: Yes, Jon, we had 14 new stores this year, and we're looking at probably 8 -- in the range of 8 next year. And we've been very happy with the openings this year starting out. The stores look great, traveling the stores, the product and the teams are ready for holiday, and we're excited about what everybody is doing in the stores and the support staff.

    Jon Braatz: Dennis, obviously, over the last -- this past year and this next year, your store growth has accelerated after sort of a low period. What are you seeing in terms of the environment? And since they gave us the opportunity to run our regular stores and open up in their outlets, we found it to be a great combination. They're in communities that a lot of people know us or they're tourists that hit those spots. And so that's given us kind of a whole new lineup to review for opening stores, and we've been very excited about it.

    10 stocks we like better than Constellium Se ›.

    On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Constellium (CSTM -4.20%) raised its full-year outlook after delivering record third-quarter adjusted EBITDA, or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Long-term investors should care because expansion projects in high-margin aerospace and recycling are building structural earnings power.

    Three takeaways from the call highlight what matters for long-term shareholders.

    Aerospace manufacturers are accelerating production to meet massive order books, driving demand for high-value aluminum components. Constellium is expanding its capacity to capture tight market conditions and renegotiate contracts at higher prices.

    Recent findings suggest that management is executing targeted capital expenditures, or investments in physical facilities, to expand output in premium product lines. The ramp-up of latest recycling and casting facilities supports higher margins while reducing exposure to raw material price fluctuations.

    Import tariffs and trade policies are making foreign aluminum more expensive in North America, favoring domestic producers. Constellium is capitalizing on this shift through higher local demand, improved scrap metal margins, and stronger pricing in its Transportation, Industry, and Defense segment.

    Operational momentum remains elevated across key end markets as disciplined cost controls offset persistent labor and freight inflation. Management is expanding plate capacity for defense and semiconductor manufacturing while focusing on pricing discipline and balance sheet strength.

    With leverage near the bottom of its target range and latest capacity coming online, the business is structured to capture durable secular demand.

    Latest Update: Premier League KMI Panel unanimously admits to another refereeing error which wronged Liverpool

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.
    • The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.
    • The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has adjudged that Liverpool had a penalty wrongly given against them in a recent fixture.

    The Reds won their last game before the international break, beating Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, although Alisson Becker was denied a clean sheet by a stoppage-time spot kick awarded to the home side and converted by Eddie Nketiah.

    The penalty was awarded for what referee Tony Harrington deemed to be a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio when the two players unfortunately clashed heads, and Andoni Iraola mentioned afterwards that he was ‘very upset‘ over that decision.

    The Premier League’s KMI Panel has now published its findings from the most recent top-flight matchday (via premierleague.com), and all five independent assessors adjudged that the penalty award against Liverpool was incorrect.

    However, there was also unanimous agreement that VAR was right not to intervene, as it was decreed that no ‘clear and obvious’ error had taken place.

    The panel concluded: ‘The panel unanimously felt that the referee’s call of a penalty for a challenge by Kerkez on Osorio was incorrect, with the contact being inevitable given the jumping actions of both players.

    ‘However, the non-intervention of VAR was supported on the basis it was not a clear and obvious error.’.

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Liverpool fans must be getting sick of hearing from the Premier League’s KMI Panel at this stage, with this incident coming fresh off the back of the panel ruling that we should’ve had a penalty for Jurrien Timber’s blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the 0-1 defeat to Arsenal.

    Recent findings suggest that the incident with Kerkez and Osorio wasn’t as black-and-white, but the decision to award a spot kick still felt rather curious at the time. Luckily for Harrington, it came too late to have any major bearing on the overall result at Selhurst Park.

    Still, to hear that an independent panel unanimously acknowledged that the Reds were wronged by another refereeing error is galling for everyone associated with LFC, and yet again it calls into question the standads of officiating in the Premier League.

    It’s the kind of inconsistency between Kerkez having a spot kick given against him for a 50/50 duel, and Timber getting away with a blatant infringement, which drives players, coaches, fans and pundits absolutely berserk.

    Thankfully the decision in the Palace game didn’t do any lasting harm for Liverpool, but you get the sense that it won’t be long before another contentious decision goes against us and the KPI Panel is wheeled out to tell us what we can already deduce for ourselves.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -6.19%) is arguably the top space stock on the market today.
    • In a recent development, if you're also looking to profit from the space race, the best strategy may not be to invest directly in space stocks.
    • For decades, investors have considered Tesla (TSLA -6.92%) an automotive stock.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 20, 2026 at 1:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    Sources indicate that space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -6.19%) is arguably the top space stock on the market today. But it's far from the only one. There are dozens of companies directly profiting from today's space race. But there are hundreds more that will benefit in more indirect ways.

    In a recent development, if you're also looking to profit from the space race, the best strategy may not be to invest directly in space stocks. Instead, look for companies with ways to benefit that aren't fully appreciated by the market. With this in mind, one trillion-dollar business stands out.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:15 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For decades, investors have considered Tesla (TSLA -6.92%) an automotive stock. That paradigm is no longer true. Tesla's $1.5 trillion valuation has little to do with making cars. Instead, that valuation is tied to future growth opportunities, with robotaxis at the top of the list.

    At first glance, robotaxis don't seem to be directly related to space. But if you understand the value and limitations of autonomous driving technology, the connection becomes clear.

    Robotaxis are widely believed to be a multi-trillion-dollar opportunity. With the ability to manufacture its own cars, Tesla has both a scaling and cost advantage over its competitors, many of which lack internal manufacturing capabilities.

    Tesla intends on leveraging these advantages by launching its own robotaxi platform. In effect, the manufacturer could become the Uber Technologies (UBER -1.13%) of robotaxis, albeit while operating a closed ecosystem exclusively for Tesla models.

    At the top of the list is connectivity.

    "Autonomous driving will increasingly demand more and more reliable network-based structures, requiring redundant, real-time architectures," concludes a report from the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers. "Car manufacturers will be required to continuously increase bandwidths for both point-to-point data pipes and distributed network structures to meet fresh data demands. Level 5 cars will send 25 gigabytes of data to the cloud every hour.".

    It has been revealed that in other words, robotaxis will require huge amounts of bandwidth to operate. If a robotaxi relies solely on terrestrial data networks, it creates connectivity vulnerabilities. That could cause service outages, customer experience problems, or even safety challenges. Network redundancy will matter. That's exactly the value that Starlink can provide for Tesla.

    "We can't have Robotaxis getting stuck in these Bermuda Triangles of lack of cellular connectivity," Elon Musk warned investors earlier this year. "There are many places, even in Silicon Valley, where the cellular coverage is terrible or sometimes non-existent, which is surprising for Silicon Valley. I know when I drive to work, those first 10, 15 minutes, I can't actually do any calls because the cellular connectivity is so bad ... Starlink with its ability to do connectivity anywhere is actually quite important, so we don't have Robotaxis missing in action.".

    Robotaxis are a huge component of Tesla's current valuation. The total robotaxi opportunity could ultimately be valued at more than Tesla's market cap today. Robotaxi execution will therefore be critical, and the tech giant's close relationship with SpaceX and Starlink should ultimately make it an unlikely winner of today's space race.

    Tech Report: Ray Dalio claims Bessent move is sign that a debt crisis is getting closer; recommends gold and bitcoin

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's proposal to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio remarked. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    According to recent reports, bessent said in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    In a recent development, after years of overspending, Dalio stated total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    Industry observers note that to solve this, Dalio mentioned the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    First, Dalio mentioned the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the New York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    Sources indicate that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio said. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he stated.

    Dalio said it's key to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder said.

    In a recent development, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Here's What the Average Social Security Benefit Actually Covers

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:00PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that most retirees lean on Social Security for much of their income, yet the average check was built to replace only part of a paycheck.
    • According to recent reports, that amounts to $25,106.04 per year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:00PM EST.

    Industry observers note that most retirees lean on Social Security for much of their income, yet the average check was built to replace only part of a paycheck. As of October 2026, the average monthly benefit for a retired worker is $2,092.17, according to the Social Security Administration (SSA).

    According to recent reports, that amounts to $25,106.04 per year. While this provides a predictable stream of income, it's often significantly less than what you'll need to maintain your standard of living after you stop working.

    A household headed by someone age 65 or older spends an average of $61,432 per year, according to the 2024 Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Consumer Expenditure Survey. While housing and healthcare are major line items, costs such as transportation and food also consume a large share of the budget.

    According to recent reports, the table below breaks down these annual costs for senior households. Note that these expenses are compared against benefit figures as of October 2026.

    That $25,106.04 average annual benefit covers only 41% of typical senior household spending. This gap exists by design, as Social Security is built to replace roughly 40% of your pre-retirement income. The benefit formula is the same for everyone and is meant to be a foundation, not a full budget.

    The SSA bases your benefit on an average of your 35 highest-earning years, where earlier wages are adjusted for inflation and run through the primary insurance amount (PIA) formula. This results in an average yearly shortfall of $36,325.96 that retirees must cover through savings, a pension, or other income.

    For those without a pension or deep savings, part-time work may be the only realistic choice to bridge that gap. A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027, adding about $75 a month to the average benefit.

    These adjustments are designed to help your buying power keep pace with inflation, though they aren't intended to close the structural gap between your benefits and your total expenses. The average check remains a foundation for your retirement income, but the challenge for most is finding the right way to cover the rest.

    Industry observers note that personal savings are the best option to pay for what Social Security won't cover. It doesn't matter whether you keep these funds in a 401(k), an IRA, or even a health savings account (HSA), so long as they're accessible to you when you need them.

    According to recent reports, if you qualify for a pension through your employer, this may also go a long way toward covering your remaining expenses. Talk to your employer to get a rough idea of how much your pension might offer you in monthly or annual income in retirement.

    Recent findings suggest that when personal savings aren't enough, and a pension isn't an option, you might have to explore alternatives, like working in retirement. It might not be ideal, but there are plenty of flexible options these days that enable you to work from home or set your own hours, so you should still have plenty of time to enjoy some of the freedoms of retirement.

    For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

    • Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining newly introduced traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases declared so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," remarked Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    In a recent development, the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    Recent findings suggest that the Treasury Department said last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "massive toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah said. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah noted. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah noted in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Sources indicate that deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder remarked.

    In a recent development, "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that cerebras Systems (CBRS -0.44%) continued to rebound from its lows, climbing 11% on Nov.
    • Industry observers note that cerebras, which makes systems built around its wafer-scale chips the size of an iPad, has thus far been more of a niche provider of high-end artificial intelligence inference (AI) systems with a small customer base.
    • It has been revealed that in addition to the substantial deal with Microsoft, Cerebras also addressed rumors around OpenAI, which is set to become its largest customer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Cerebras Systems ›.

    Industry observers note that cerebras Systems (CBRS -0.44%) continued to rebound from its lows, climbing 11% on Nov. 13 after the stock reported soaring revenue and confirmed a deal with Microsoft (MSFT -1.97%). However, the semiconductor stock is still down more than 40% from its $185 IPO price in May, and more than 70% off its highs.

    Industry observers note that cerebras, which makes systems built around its wafer-scale chips the size of an iPad, has thus far been more of a niche provider of high-end artificial intelligence inference (AI) systems with a small customer base. As such, the deal with Microsoft is vital, as Cerebras continues to expand its client list, which now includes OpenAI, Amazon (AMZN -3.32%), and Oracle (ORCL -6.98%). As the manufacturer's systems move into the mainstream, it still looks like a good time to buy the stock.

    It has been revealed that in addition to the substantial deal with Microsoft, Cerebras also addressed rumors around OpenAI, which is set to become its largest customer. It noted that it didn't have enough capacity to provide the system behind OpenAI's ultra-fast mode for its latest models, and that this was why its solution wasn't used, not for technical reasons.

    NASDAQ · As of 2:12 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Cerebras has a take-or-pay contract with OpenAI worth more than $20 billion for 750 megawatts of capacity, accounted for in its remaining performance obligations (RPOs), which total $26.1 billion as of the end of September. Notably, the Oracle and Microsoft deals were signed after the quarter and are not in that amount. Due to delays, Cerebras may owe OpenAI delay credits, which were deducted from its RPOs.

    According to recent reports, despite some hiccups with OpenAI, Cerebras saw its revenue jump 55% to $210.8 million. Its core sales figure, which strips out revenue distortions from customer warrants and pass-through accounting, soared 70% to $230.9 million, topping the $214.7 million consensus, as compiled by LSEG.

    Customers continue to prefer renting its systems, leading to its cloud revenue climbing 265% year over year to $141.9 million and its core cloud revenue surging 287% to $144.9 million. Hardware revenue sank 29% year over year to $68.9 million, while core hardware revenue slipped 11% to $86 million.

    According to recent reports, gross margins have been an matter for Cerebras. Its core gross margins came in at 41%, up 30 basis points versus a year ago. Core gross margin for its cloud operation was 46.9%, a significant improvement from 16.5% a year ago. However, its core hardware gross margin was 31%, down from 50.5% a year ago. The organization said this was due to the continued ramp of its manufacturing capabilities and the final shipments of hardware to early customers under special pricing. Its long-term target for hardware gross margins is 60%. Meanwhile, its cloud gross margins were impacted by Cerebras renting back some equipment from a customer.

    Management projected Q4 core revenue of between $310 million and $330 million, with core gross margins between 47% and 49%. Cerebras also raised its full-year guidance, taking its core revenue forecast to a range of $940 million to $960 million, up from a previous outlook of $880 million to $890 million. It now sees its core gross margins coming in between 42% and 44%, up from an earlier projection between 41% and 43%.

    In a recent development, for 2027, management expects core revenue to more than triple, with strong growth for both cloud and hardware. The Microsoft deal will contribute revenue starting in the first half of the year, and Oracle's will start in the summer. Cerebras anticipates substantially increasing its data center capacity next year.

    Industry observers note that cerebras has the fastest inference solution, which is growing faster than the AI model training market and is expected to become the larger of the two markets in the coming years. In fact, Bloomberg Intelligence projects the inference market will be double the size of the training market by 2032.

    In a recent development, cerebras has arguably the best inference solution; the issue is that it's expensive. Still, the company is making inroads and gaining big, newly introduced customers. While it's seen some hiccups with capacity, it has a long runway for growth.

    While I consider Cerebras stock speculative, I think it looks like a buy at these levels, given its potential to disrupt the chip market in inference.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, at the time of this writing (around noon on Nov.
    • But is today's share price really a bargain?
    • Archer is developing an electric air taxi, which it calls Midnight.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 20, 2026 at 2:30PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Archer Aviation ›.

    According to recent reports, at the time of this writing (around noon on Nov. 16), Archer Aviation (ACHR -8.75%) stock is trading below $4 a share. That's a seemingly remarkable price for a company with ambitions to revolutionize urban transportation, especially considering its stock was flying high in the double digits just last year.

    But is today's share price really a bargain? And if so, could a $5,000 investment today be enough to set you up for life?

    NYSE · As of 2:14 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Archer is developing an electric air taxi, which it calls Midnight. It doesn't have regulatory approval to fly its eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) commercially (no one has that certificate in the U.S.), but it is widely considered one of the frontrunners in this nascent industry.

    What the heck is an air taxi? Basically, a cross between a helicopter, an airplane, and a drone. This feat of engineering can take off vertically like a helicopter, then switch to forward flight like an airplane, cruising at speeds of up to 150 mph. If it gets all the necessary approvals, it could radically change how people travel, turning hour-long traffic jams into urban hops that last minutes.

    Industry observers note that how close is Archer to getting its approval ducks in order? Closer than ever, but not quite ready for takeoff. Indeed, the company has entered the fourth and final phase of the FAA's type certification process. "Final" sounds encouraging, but this phase is not for the faint of heart. It involves rigorous testing to prove that Midnight can carry passengers safely, with regulators scrutinizing everything from the flight's performance to its safety systems. The process could take years. There's no guarantee Midnight will make it through.

    If Midnight does make it through, the long-term opportunity could be enormous. Morgan Stanley (MS -4.04%) has estimated that the global eVTOL market could reach $255 billion by 2035 and $1 trillion by 2040. Archer doesn't need to capture the entire market to grow substantially; even a small slice could translate into billions in annual revenue.

    Let's play with some numbers. At $4 a share, a $5,000 investment would buy you 1,250 shares. If the stock were to climb tenfold, that investment would be worth $50,000. A 20-fold increase would make your shares worth $100,000, and a 50-fold increase would be worth $250,000.

    Industry observers note that so, yes, on paper, the potential returns are enormous. On the other hand, all of them would require Archer to develop into a major player in the aviation industry, with a thriving air taxi business, substantial revenue, and, eventually, consistent profits.

    According to recent reports, can Archer do that? Maybe, maybe not. And it's precisely the uncertainty behind that "maybe" that helps explain why Archer trades at $4 a share, not, say, $14. Risk-tolerant, intrepid investors might be interested in Archer at this price, but those averse to risk might want to avoid the eVTOL industry for now.

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    Neocloud organization CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    It has been revealed that chatterjee said CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    In a recent development, "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," said Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Recent findings suggest that chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    After a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    Over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and newly introduced markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security organization, Powell mentioned. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell stated.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    Sources indicate that powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he mentioned.

    In a recent development, devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    Overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the manufacturer if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he mentioned. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    According to recent reports, "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.
